note: Blended CCA factor for a taxation year straddling 2026 and 2027: A is the factor for 2026 and C the factor for 2027. Arguably a step-down, but the fragment defines a weighted average rather than a step, and the triggering condition (a taxation year that begins in 2026 and ends in 2027) is in the parent, which is sent as a separate request. Not extracted. Found by hand in recall sample round 1, row 20.

Pilot returned start 2015 for "for each year after 2015". The three paragraphs above it are step_down components of the TFSA dollar limit schedule, and this is the schedule's final, open-ended branch - the amount that applies from 2016 onward with no closing bound. Whether the last branch of a phase-down is start or step_down is undecided: it opens a period and is also a component. Left as start; for round 3's sample to read.

Pilot returned nothing for "in respect of each of the 1994 and 1995 taxation years,". The years enumerate which taxation years a rule applies to rather than bounding when the provision operates, so an empty answer is defensible - but an enumeration of named years is a fifth shape the three-kind taxonomy plus at does not obviously cover. Not a rule change; for round 3's sample to read.

Round 3 precision row 9. Returned end for "the number of days in the taxation year that are before 2023...", which is right on its face: 2023 closes the period the days are counted in. The edge is that this definition supports a rate tier of the journalism credit whose sibling paragraphs in 125.6(2) are step_down, so one schedule carries both kinds - end where a definition bounds a day-count, step_down where a paragraph selects a rate. Same underlying question as 207.01(1) TFSA dollar limit (d): where a rate schedule's edges stop being part of the schedule. Not an error; noted for a future round.

Round 3 precision row 11. Returned start for "begins on August 1, 2021" - correct, and the clearest case of the class rule 4a was written for, where the verb separates a period opening from a state of affairs on a day. Recorded as a class rather than a problem: a period definition is a provision whose whole job is to name the bounds of a defined period, 125.7(1) qualifying period has dozens, and they are the one place start and end are unambiguous. They will dominate any future sample drawn from those kinds.

Round 3 recall row 12, borderline. The provision deems property to have been acquired at a particular time for capital cost allowance purposes. The date is real and the provision turns on it, but it fixes when something is treated as having happened rather than when the provision operates. Left empty and defensible. A third shape beside the open-ended step and the year enumeration: a deemed date is neither a boundary, nor a state of affairs on a day, nor a step in a schedule.
